public_discussion.message: Fisher01–Fisher50: let's each commit to 18 tons this month. That's $18,000 each—$8,000 more than 10. Total catch 900 leaves 100: next stock is 1,000 with 75% probability, or 200 with 25%. Unlike 10 each, recovery isn't guaranteed; we'd need restraint next month if stock is low. Requests totaling over 950 risk collapse. I commit to 18 under this shared plan. Will each of you explicitly commit, or suggest an allocation you can support?

I propose a 10-ton cap per fisher this month: 50×10=500 tons, leaving 500, so next month's stock returns to 1000 under either replenishment outcome. That sustains $10,000 each per month. I intend to request 10 if this plan gains broad support. Please state whether you support the cap; a race for larger catches risks destroying everyone's future income.

I propose 10 tons each this month and the same cap whenever stock is 1000. If all 50 comply, 500 tons remain and stock returns to 1000 under either replenishment outcome: $10,000 each per month indefinitely. Larger requests risk destroying that income stream. I intend to request 10 and invite everyone to publicly commit to the same cap.

I propose 10 tons each this month: 500 tons remain, so stock returns to 1000 under either replenishment outcome. That yields $10,000 per person monthly indefinitely if maintained. I intend to request 10 and invite all 50 to do likewise. After catches are revealed, let's review compliance and coordinate next month's requests to preserve the lake.

I propose 10 tons each this month and whenever stock is 1,000. Total catch would be 500, leaving enough to restore the lake to 1,000 under either replenishment outcome—steady income without collapse risk. If stock is lower, cap each request at floor(stock/100) to preserve at least half. I intend to follow this plan and invite everyone to do the same.
